prop:torus-knot-delta-q-writhe:
Proposition Writhe exponent of the torus-knot \delta_q decoration: \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = h\,[(m-1)p]_q. For the torus knot T_{m,p} presented on the minimal number of strands — that is, with m \leq p, so that m is the braid index (Morton–Williams) — the top-channel decoration is h times the quantum integer at the writhe w = (m-1)p:

  \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) \;=\; q^{w} - q^{-w} \;=\; h\,[w]_q.

By definition the decoration is the bar-odd part of the top-channel twist q^{w}; the content of the statement is the factorisation q^{w} - q^{-w} = h\,[w]_q. The writhe exponent governs the h\,[w]_q form across all torus knots, matching the 10_{124} = T_{3,5} and 8_{19} = T_{3,4} force-carrier evaluations.

The minimal-strand condition is not cosmetic. prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot:
Proposition Pole order at q=0 of the torus-knot character: \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{p,k}) = k(p-1) on V_{(1^p)}. Let p \geq 1, k \geq 1 with \gcd(p, k) = 1, and let T_{p,k} be the (p, k)-torus knot, presented as the closure of the braid \beta_{p,k} = (\sigma_1 \sigma_2 \cdots \sigma_{p-1})^k \in B_p. Define the shift exponent of the braid \beta_{p,k}

  \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(\beta_{p,k})
  \;:=\;
  \max_{\lambda \,\vdash\, p}\;
  \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}^{(-)}\; \chi_\lambda(\beta_{p,k})

where \chi_\lambda is the seminormal Hecke character on V_\lambda (q-dimension decoration \delta_q) and \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}^{(-)} denotes the pole order at q = 0 (i.e. the negative of the Laurent valuation). Then:

  1. The channel V_{(1^p)} has pole order exactly k(p-1).
  2. For (p, k) \in \{(2,3), (2,5), (2,9), (3,4), (3,5), (3,7)\} this channel is the maximizer, so \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(\beta_{p,k}) = k(p - 1) for those pairs. For general (p, k) maximality is conjectural.

\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} is an invariant of the braid \beta_{p,k}, not of the knot T_{p,k}: since T_{p,k} \cong T_{k,p}, the two braid presentations give k(p-1) and p(k-1), which differ when p \neq k (for the trefoil, 3 from \beta_{2,3} and 4 from \beta_{3,2}). The notation \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{p,k}) is retained elsewhere only as shorthand for \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(\beta_{p,k}) with p the braid index.

prf:alpha-shift-torus-knot:
Proof Proof of alpha shift torus knot. On V_{(1^p)} (closed-form contribution).

The single SYT of shape (1^p) fills the column with entries 1, 2, \ldots, p from top to bottom, giving cell contents 0, -1, -2, \ldots, -(p-1) and axial-distance pattern \rho_i = c(i+1) - c(i) = -1 for every consecutive pair (i, i+1).

In the Hoefsmit construction, axial distance \rho = -1 is a 1 \times 1 block with eigenvalue a_{-1} = h / (1 - q^{2}) which simplifies (after the \det = -1 normalisation) to -q^{-1}. Hence each \sigma_i acts as the scalar -q^{-1} on V_{(1^p)}, and

  \chi_{(1^p)}(\beta_{p,k})
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl[(-q^{-1})^{k(p-1)} \cdot I\bigr]
  \;=\;
  (-1)^{k(p-1)} \, q^{-k(p-1)}.

This is a single Laurent monomial with pole order exactly k(p - 1) at q = 0. There is no within-partition cancellation because the SYT path visits distinct axial distances at every step (no adjacent contents differ by \pm 1), so the b^2 = (1 - q^{2\rho - 2})(1 - q^{2\rho + 2})/(1 - q^{2\rho})^2 zeroing on adjacent contents in the 2 \times 2 Hoefsmit blocks never fires on V_{(1^p)}.

The maximality claim — that no other \lambda \vdash p achieves pole order > k(p - 1) — is verified case-by-case in the canonical formalism for (p, k) \in \{(2, 3), (2, 5), (2, 9), (3, 4), (3, 5), (3, 7)\}: in every case the trivial-channel V_{(p)} gives pole order 0 (it acts by the eigenvalue q, contributing q^{k(p-1)}, no pole), and the mixed V_{(p-1, 1)}, V_{(p-2, 2)}, \ldots channels give pole order \leq 0 as well, so the maximum is realised uniquely at V_{(1^p)}.

A general proof would establish that for the cyclic torus braid \beta_{p,k}, the rank of the -q^{-1} eigenspace contribution strictly increases as \lambda becomes more "column-like" in the dominance order. This is conjectured to follow directly via the Schur–Weyl pole-counting (each row of \lambda contributes one +q eigenvalue per Coxeter cycle, each column one -q^{-1}), but defer the categorical argument to a separate proposition.

prop:crystal-r-matrix-sub-lemma:
Proposition Crystal R-matrix Sub-lemma 2.1: pole order of the seminormal diagonal entry. Let \mathbf{H}_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field with q generic, \lambda \vdash n, and \beta_1 \in \mathbf{H}_{n_1}(q), \beta_2 \in \mathbf{H}_{n_2}(q) with n = n_1 + n_2. Let \sigma_i \in \mathbf{H}_n(q) be a boundary generator and let A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(\sigma_i) be its (\mu, \nu)-block in the Wenzl LR decomposition. For a standard Young tableau T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda) in the (\mu, \nu)-block, let \rho_T(i) = c(i+1) - c(i) be the axial distance, with c = \mathrm{col} - \mathrm{row} the content of the cell holding the entry.

The diagonal entry of A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(\sigma_i) at T has pole order at q = 0

  \boxed{\;\;
    \mathrm{pole}\bigl(A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(\sigma_i),\, T\bigr)
    \;=\;
    \mathbf{1}\bigl[\rho_T(i) \le -1\bigr].
  \;\;}

In Hoefsmit's seminormal form [hoefsmit1974] the boundary generator acts on the basis vector v_T with diagonal entry

  a_T(i) \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{1 - q^{-2\rho}}, \qquad \rho = \rho_T(i),

which is -q^{-1} on a column tableau (\rho = -1) and q on a row tableau (\rho = 1). For \rho = -(m+1),

  a_T(i) \;=\; q^{-1}\,\frac{q^2 - 1}{1 - q^{2(m+1)}},

and the second factor takes the value -1 at q = 0, so the pole is simple. For \rho = m+1,

  a_T(i) \;=\; q^{2m+1}\,\frac{q^2 - 1}{q^{2(m+1)} - 1},

and the second factor takes the value 1 at q = 0, so there is no pole. Both factorisations hold over any field.

The statement concerns the diagonal entry only; the off-diagonal entries of the seminormal form are not covered. The column-tableau count it gives, k(p-1) poles for (\sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{p-1})^k on V_{(1^p)}, is checked for seven torus-knot interfaces and six non-column shapes.

def:lp-duality-hypothesis-class:
Definition Finite LP strong-duality + complementary-slackness hypothesis class (§3b-cond). An operator-selection LP, given by its objective t, Gram matrix G, net target n_{\mathrm{target}} and box bound M, satisfies the finite LP-duality hypothesis if it has a primal-feasible point x and a dual-feasible point (y_0, y, w) with zero duality gap.

Complementary slackness then follows: a constraint with positive shadow price y_\lambda > 0 is tight, (Gx)_\lambda = 0. The converse, that every tight constraint has positive shadow price, is strict complementarity (Goldman–Tucker). It holds for some optimal pair but not for every one, so it is a separate hypothesis.

This isolates the standard finite-dimensional LP strong-duality and complementary-slackness theorems, which are cited rather than re-proved here, as an explicit hypothesis. Results that rely on them are stated conditional on it; discharging it changes no downstream mathematical commitment.

That identity is unstratified — it equates the whole transient trace with the whole dilogarithm and says nothing about levels. The level-by-level refinement this step needs is partition-depth stratification of \Phi_q, and with it the analytic representation of the curvature-rank-k stratum on the i-th exceptional divisor is

  \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}\big|_{i\text{-th divisor}}
  \;=\;
  \bigl[\Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) - \Phi_q^{[\leq k-1]}(z_i)\bigr],

where \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z) = \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1 - q^{-j}z)^{-1} is the depth-k truncation. Telescoping the sum over k = 0, \ldots, k_\star(T_w) gives

  \sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(T_w)} \alpha_k \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}\big|_i
  \;=\;
  \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i),

The brane-tower contribution from the i-th divisor is \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i), a finite product of k_\star(T_w) factors.

Step 5 (truncation invariance for k \geq k_\star). For any k \geq k_\star(T_w), the additional factors (1 - q^{-j}z)^{-1} for j > k_\star(T_w) correspond by Step 4 to strata Z^{(j)}(A) with j > k_\star(T_w), on which T_w has zero projection by definition of k_\star. Therefore

  \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{proj}_{\mathrm{supp}(T_w)}
  \;=\;
  \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{proj}_{\mathrm{supp}(T_w)}

inside Z(A), where \mathrm{proj}_{\mathrm{supp}(T_w)} projects onto the NF-support stratum. Combined with Step 1's vanishing E_\infty^{\geq 1, *} = 0, this gives the corollary: any k \geq k_\star(T_w) yields the same categorical brane-tower contribution. \square

Proof gap closure (partial). The structural bridge for Step 4 — identifying the level-k factor of \Phi_q with the depth-k centre stratum — is now provided by partition-depth stratification of \Phi_q. That proposition gives the depth-k Frobenius-dual coefficients \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \in Z^{(k)}(A) such that the partial product \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) = \sum_{j \leq k} \phi_q^{(j)}(z_i) on the nose, and the truncation identity

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr)

holds as a Frobenius-paired equality, derived from depth-orthogonality under the Frobenius pairing on Z(A).

Remaining gap (canonical, not structural). The Frobenius-paired identity above is a categorical equality: the sums \sum_k \langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i), T_w \rangle and the analytic \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w) agree as elements of R. To conclude that the canonical mass formula at q = q_0 with \Phi_q replaced by \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]} gives the same real-valued answer, one needs the depth-k projections \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}}(\Phi_q(z_i)) to be uniformly bounded as |z_i| \to q. The analytic infinite product diverges in this limit; the Frobenius-paired identity says that whatever divergent content \Phi_q(z_i) accumulates above depth k_\star(T_w) pairs to zero with T_w, but the uniform canonical bound on the truncated remainder is the open part — the conjectural target of z-Habiro completion.

The structural content of the proposition — that the brane tower is centre-stratified, truncates categorically at a finite depth k_\star(T_w) structurally determined by NF support, and the analytic \Phi_q infinite product is a faithful Frobenius-pairing representation up to the depth-k_\star truncation — is closed modulo the depth-stratified version of \Phi_q (conj:quantum-dilogarithm-stratified). The remaining gap is between the categorical equality and its real-valued canonical evaluation at |\hat{V}|\approx 1.

Comparison, not part of the proof. The empirical k=2 subtractive cut-off (brane-tower in z-Habiro §"Empirical observation") for D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He} is not supported by this argument: with GB-depth fixed as the a-function, k_\star(T_w)=\binom n2, and under the max-hook depth k_\star(T_w)=n; neither is \le 2 at the relevant n. Scope of Steps 4–5. Steps 4–5 together assert that the level-K partial sum equals \sum_i\Phi_q^{[\le K]}(z_i) for every K and is constant for K\ge k_\star. Proof Proof of plancherel weight boundedness. Proof. The classical Plancherel identity for the symmetric-group regular representation, lifted to the Hecke algebra via the Wedderburn--Artin decomposition (Wedderburn trace):

  \dim_\mathbb{Q} A \;=\; n!

(The Hecke irrep dimensions \dim V_\lambda are q-independent for generic q — they coincide with the symmetric-group irrep dimensions f_\lambda.) Dividing by n! proves (2). Each summand is a non-negative ratio bounded by the total sum, proving (1). \square

The total mass functional \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{T}) = \sum_k \alpha_k \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{T}) is therefore absolutely convergent for any bounded |\alpha_k|, with no super-exponential divergence at large n.

prf:spectral-sequence-collapse:
Proof Proof of spectral sequence collapse. Proof. A separable algebra has \mathrm{HH}^k(A, M) = 0 for k \geq 1 and every bimodule M (Hochschild 1945; this is the associative analogue of Whitehead's lemma, not Whitehead's lemma itself). A semisimple algebra over a field of characteristic zero is separable. The spectral sequence E_r^{p, q} \Rightarrow \mathrm{HH}^{p+q} then has E_\infty^{p,q} = 0 for p + q \geq 1, and E_\infty^{0, 0} = \mathrm{HH}^0 = Z(A). Nothing here forces the differentials d_r to vanish. \square

Corollary (mass functional is a q-deformed Wedderburn-weighted centre projection). The categorical mass functional pairs the Frobenius integral \int_A : A \to R with the centre via the Wedderburn decomposition (categorical mass, Markov):

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n} w_\lambda(q) \cdot \frac{\chi_\lambda(\rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}))}{\dim_q V_\lambda},
  \qquad w_\lambda(q) = \frac{\dim_q^2 V_\lambda}{[n]_q!},

The q-deformed Wedderburn weights w_\lambda(q) are bounded, but \sum w_\lambda(q) \neq 1 at q \neq 1 in general (cf. Plancherel weights define a probability distribution: \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1, 0 \leq w_\lambda \leq 1 for the classical Plancherel measure w_\lambda(1) = (\dim V_\lambda)^2/n! that does sum to 1). Binning by GB-depth (curvature-rank stratification) gives the curvature-rank decomposition \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}} = \sum_k \alpha_k \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(1) (unified mass formula).

Frobenius duality of strata. The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle = \int_A a \cdot b gives a self-duality A \cong A^{\vee} (Yekutieli rigidity). Under this duality the GB filtration J^0 \supset J^1 \supset \cdots \supset J^N maps to its annihilator filtration

  (J^\ell)^\perp \;=\; \{a : {\textstyle\int_A}\, a \cdot J^\ell = 0\} \;=\; J^{N - \ell}.

This is Poincaré duality of curvature-rank strata: rank-\ell contributions pair with rank-(N - \ell) contributions under the Frobenius integral. The chirality stratum (S-anti-invariant rank \geq 2) is self-dual under combined S-reversal and rank inversion.

Refuted on the centre, scope (b). The sentence above transports the annihilator duality from A to the strata, and the paragraph below reads those strata off the central idempotents e_\lambda. On that basis the pairing is diagonal, not anti-diagonal, so distinct strata pair to zero: for any linear functional \varphi, \varphi(e_\lambda e_\mu) = \varphi(\delta_{\lambda\mu} e_\lambda). Measured exactly in \mathbb{Q}(q) at n = 3 on the corpus's own idempotents — all six off-diagonal entries identically 0, diagonal \mathrm{diag}(\tau(e_\lambda)) nonzero, completeness self-test \sum_\lambda \tau(e_\lambda) = 1. So each stratum is self-dual and the annihilator of a stratum within Z is the span of the complementary idempotents — a set complement, not a rank-reindexed stratum. The asserted pairing is identically zero exactly where it claims to be perfect, whenever \ell \neq N - \ell.

Scope (b) rests on a proved invariant — mutual annihilation of distinct central primitive idempotents — which holds for every linear functional and every n. So no choice of filtration and no choice of Frobenius form restores a cross-stratum pairing here, and supplying the missing J^\bullet bridge would not repair it: this defect is independent of the Gap note below.

Not refuted: (J^\ell)^\perp = J^{N - \ell} as a statement about the filtration of A itself, which is a different claim and is untouched here; and the Practical consequence below, which uses the Wedderburn sum and not this duality. Same defect as Partial argument for the stratified quantum dilogarithm Step 1.

Practical consequence. categorical derivation steps need only enumerate central idempotents e_\lambda, compute their GB-depth, evaluate \chi_\lambda via Hoefsmit seminormal form (Hoefsmit pipeline), and sum \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta) / \dim_q V_\lambda binning by \mathrm{depth}(\lambda). This uses only the centre Z(A) = E_\infty^{0,0}, so no page of the spectral sequence is needed. That is not because the differentials d_r vanish, which is not shown.

Gap. The step above reads a grading of the centre by partition depth off a proposition that stratifies H_n(R,q) by the curvature rank of words. That identification is not stated in the cited proposition, and the three readings of J^\bullet present in the corpus are each excluded: the ideal-power reading is provably \bot above degree 0 ; the Coxeter-length reading fails a dimension count at n \leq 3; and the rewrite-depth reading is identically zero once the Hecke normal form fixes T_w as the unique normal-form basis indexed by S_n. Not claimed: that this block's conclusion is false — only that the step it rests on is unestablished, and that the obvious ways to establish it do not work.

Proof Proof of plancherel term 7 formulation. Each \{\lambda : \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) = k\} is finite, so each \Phi_k is a finite R-valued sum. By curvature-rank stratification, the central idempotent e_\lambda has GB-filtration depth \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) — assumed, not established; see the gap note below — so binning \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \log|\int_{A_\lambda} \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \cdot \mathcal{T}| by \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) is the canonical curvature-rank decomposition of the (logarithmic) Frobenius pairing. The threshold k \geq 4 is determined by which strata of Z(H_n(R, q)) still carry a distinguished knot ideal — empirically k_* = 4.

The total sum is bounded: \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda(q) is finite for every n and equals 1 exactly at q = 1; at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps) it deviates from 1 — categorically \sum w_\lambda(q) \approx 1.51 at n = 12 (prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness remark on q-deformed alternative). Boundedness of \Phi_k follows from finiteness of the w_\lambda(q) together with finiteness of the per-block log-Frobenius pairings; the absolute-convergence constant is \sup_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \#\Lambda_k \cdot \sup_\lambda |\log|\!\int||, not 1 as for the classical Plancherel measure. \square

Logarithmic control of scale. The bare Wedderburn-weighted character sum \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta) / \dim_q V_\lambda is bounded by a finite constant (canonical \lesssim 2 at q_0 for n \leq 12), giving a similarly small MeV-scale ceiling — too small for MeV-scale binding gaps. Replacing \chi_\lambda with \log|\!\int_{A_\lambda}\!\cdot| keeps the Wedderburn weighting bounded but lets each block contribute O(\log|\chi|), which can be large. This is how the formula reaches \sim 30 MeV {}^4\mathrm{He} binding from a bounded measure: logarithmic unbounding of bounded characters.

An older form of "Term 7" used the Hopf hook polynomial H_q(\lambda) = \prod_{x \in \lambda}[h_x]_q summed naively across deep partitions; that form diverges as q^{n^2/2}. thm:frobenius-codim-universal:
Theorem Universal Frobenius co-dimension trace: \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda). Let A = H_n(R, q) be a self-dual Frobenius algebra with Markov trace \tau, and suppose \tau(p_\lambda) \neq 0 for every central idempotent p_\lambda. The quantum-co-dimension element

  C_{\dim_q}
  \;:=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}}
    \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda) \cdot \tau(p_\lambda)}
    \cdot p_\lambda
  \;\in\; Z(A)

lies in the centre of A and satisfies

  \boxed{
    \tau\bigl(C_{\dim_q}\bigr)
    \;=\;
    \sum_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}} \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda)}.
  }

Scope at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). The hypothesis \tau(p_\lambda) \neq 0 fails for H_n(q) with n \geq 3 at the Markov parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). There \tau(p_\lambda) = y_\lambda\,d_\lambda, and the Ocneanu weight y_\lambda vanishes for every \lambda with three or more rows, so C_{\dim_q} is not defined. What survives is the element C^{\circ}_{\dim_q} summed over \widehat{A}^{\circ} = \{\lambda : \tau(p_\lambda) \neq 0\}, with \tau(C^{\circ}_{\dim_q}) = \sum_{\lambda \in \widehat{A}^{\circ}} 1/\dim_q(\lambda). The all-partition sum \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} 1/\dim_q(\lambda) remains defined as a formal sum, but for n \geq 3 at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) it is not \tau of any element constructed here. In the block model A = \prod_\lambda \mathrm{Mat}_{d_\lambda} with \tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda \operatorname{Tr} over a generic field, \operatorname{rad}\tau is the sum of the zero-weight blocks, C^{\circ}_{\dim_q} is central with trace independent of the lift from A/\operatorname{rad}\tau, and once a block vanishes no central element c satisfies \tau(c\,p_\lambda) = 1/\dim_q(\lambda) on every block. At z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) the surviving sum runs over the partitions with at most two rows.
